body.explanation: UDP at 2 Gbps over a 1 Gbps FIFO link keeps the queue full, so most TCP segments are tail-dropped and TCP repeatedly enters RTO backoff. Queue length and TCP type only change the rare phase in which a few segments find queue space and are acknowledged; the delivered payload is therefore an integer-segment effect, not a bandwidth-sharing effect. The best observed value is 5792 bps, tied by TcpCubic at q=1000 and q=250 and by TcpLinuxReno at q=1000, and no tested setting exceeds it by more than 1%.
